title: Letters Every Word Shares
statement:
You get a list of lowercase words. Return every letter that appears in all of them, as a list of one-letter strings.

Repeats count: if every word contains the letter e at least twice, "e" appears twice in the answer. In general a letter appears as many times as its smallest count across the words.

Any order of the result is accepted.

examples.why: Each word has at least two e's, one p and one r. "pepper" has three p's, but "peer" has only one.
No letter is in both words.
With one word, every letter of it counts, repeats included.

hints: Think in letter counts, not positions.
For one letter, how many copies can go in the answer? It is limited by the word that has the fewest.
Keep a running 26-slot array of minimum counts. Start from the first word and take the element-wise minimum with each next word's counts.

explain.intuition:
A letter can appear in the answer only as many times as the stingiest word allows. So for each of the 26 letters, the answer count is the minimum of its counts across all words. Keep one array common[26], start it from the first word's counts, and shrink it with each next word by taking the element-wise minimum.

At the end, write out each letter common[c] times. It is the same idea as intersecting two multisets, applied word after word.
steps: Count the letters of the first word into common.
For each other word, count its letters into cnt and set common[c] = min(common[c], cnt[c]).
For each letter, push it common[c] times into the result.
pitfalls: Using sets, which lose repeats: the first example needs two e's.
Starting common at all zeros and taking minimums: everything stays zero. Start from the first word, or from infinity.

solutions.title: Cross off letters from a copy
solutions.idea: Walk the letters of the first word. Keep a letter if every other word still has an unused copy of it, then cross that copy off in each word.

solutions.title: Minimum count per letter
solutions.idea: Keep the element-wise minimum of the 26 letter counts across all words, then expand it into a list.

followups: Return the letters that appear in at least half of the words instead.
The words arrive as a stream and you must answer after each one. What do you store?
